name: At what point during a bathroom or kitchen renovation is plumbing scheduled?

mainEntity.name: At what point during a bathroom or kitchen renovation is plumbing scheduled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plumbing trade coordination happens in two primary phases: the rough-in phase and the trim-out phase. After initial demolition and framing are complete, the plumbing sub-trade runs drain lines, vents, and water lines inside the open wall cavities. Once rough-in inspections are satisfied, our crew proceeds with drywall, mudding, interior painting, and tile setting. After tile and cabinetry are finished, we bring the plumbing specialist back for final trim-out to install faucets, showerheads, sinks, and toilets. This staging ensures delicate finish fixtures are not scratched or exposed to dust during major carpentry and painting work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plumbing rough-ins are scheduled immediately after framing while walls are open, and final fixture trim-out occurs after tile, cabinetry, and painting are completed.
